conclusion:
U-6 IS RESOLVED, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT RA1005-4's "(ET)" IS A TYPOGRAPHIC ERROR: the numerals in that table are CHICAGO time. Three independent CME statements settle it.

(1) RA1006-4 (NYMEX & COMEX Submission 10-306, filed 2010-10-21, advisory 2010-10-22) SUPERSEDES RA1005-4 by name and reprints the very same per-root table with EVERY time exactly one hour later under the same "(ET)" label - CLT/BZT/BBT/HOT/NGT/NNT/RBT 1:30->2:30 p.m. and 4:45->5:45 p.m.; 7FT 11:00 a.m.->12:00 p.m.; GCT 12:30->1:30 p.m.; SIT 12:25->1:25 p.m. A uniform +1h across ten rows is a zone correction, not ten independent schedule changes. The heading also changes from "Globex Pre-Open Time Period" to "Globex No-Activity Period", which is what the interval actually is: the dark window from the daily close to the next pre-open.

(2) RA1104-4 (Submission 11-131, filed 2011-03-31, advisory 2011-04-04) writes "(all times are in Eastern Time)" beside 5:46 p.m./5:16 p.m. for crude, heating oil and RBOB and 5:47/5:17 for natural gas - i.e. 16:46/16:16 and 16:47/16:17 CT.

(3) CME's own trading_hours/energy-hours.html prints BOTH columns for the TAS rows and matches RA1104-4 to the minute: "Crude Oil TAS | 17:46 ET | (16:46 CT) | 18:00-14:30 ET | (17:00-13:30 CT)" (capture 2011-11-01), "Natural Gas TAS | 17:47 ET | (16:47 CT)", "Brent Crude Oil TAS | 17:45 ET | (16:45 CT)". It also supplies the OPEN - 18:00 ET / 17:00 CT - which no MRAN edition states.

Cross-checks inside RA1005-4 itself point the same way: its GCT 12:30 p.m. and SIT 12:25 p.m. are exactly the gold and silver TAS closes the crate already holds in CT (metals hours page: "Gold TAS ... 18:00-13:30 ET (17:00-12:30)"). Read as literal ET they match nothing. And today's ContractSpecs for CL says "TAS: Sunday - Friday 5:00 p.m. - 1:30 p.m. CT". So the family's executable window - open 17:00 CT, close 13:30 CT - is unbroken from the earliest sourced statement to today, and the zone is America/Chicago.

TWO CORRECTIONS THE HANDOFF NEEDS.
(a) The handoff's "effective 2010-10-25" is WRONG. RA1006-4 keeps 2010-10-25 only for the Matched-Order half and moves the TAS half: "Effective Date November 1, 2010 (TAS Changes)" / "The prohibition will become effective on Sunday, October 31 for trade date November 1, 2010." RA1101-4, RA1102-4 and RA1104-4 all restate "On November 1, 2010, Rule 524 was amended".
(b) MORE IMPORTANTLY, I recommend NOT opening a 2010 revision row at all, and instead carrying the RA1006-4 grid back to the January-2010 floor. What became effective on 2010-10-31 was an ORDER-ENTRY PROHIBITION ("Market participants are prohibited from initiating the entry of any TAS order into Globex prior to receipt of the security status message"), which AGENTS.md's LAW-SESSION-NOT-EXPIRY expressly excludes from session evidence. The No-Activity table is labelled "provided solely for informational purposes" - it STATES the session, it does not say the session changed that day. And the pre-amendment Rule 524.A.2 ("TAS transactions on Globex may take place at any time the applicable contracts are available for trading on Globex") is a permission clause whose own redline shows CME correcting "available for trading" to "available for TAS trading" - i.e. tightening wording that had never described the Globex group structure. Reading it as "the TAS session was the full globex_energy envelope until 2010-11-01" would mint a session change out of a rule-text clarification. Carry the state back instead and record the residual risk beside the table.

THE ONE REAL DATED CHANGE in the whole chain is RA1104-4: "Effective on Sunday, April 10, 2011, for trade date Monday, April 11, 2011 ... NYMEX Light Sweet Crude Oil, New York Harbor No.2 Heating Oil and RBOB Gasoline: Monday - Thursday at 5:46 p.m., Sunday at 5:16 p.m.; NYMEX Henry Hub Natural Gas: Monday - Thursday at 5:47 p.m., Sunday at 5:17 p.m. ... The pre-open for all other TAS-eligible products ... will continue to be 5:45 p.m. ET Monday through Thursday and 5:15 p.m. ET on Sunday." That is unconditional, day-level and in session language, and it SPLITS the family three ways at minute resolution - but only in the PRE-OPEN (order_entry) window; the executable window never differed by a second. Its reversal to a flat 16:45/16:00 CT is undated (a range 16:45-16:46 by the 2013-01-16 capture, flat by 2015-03-22, randomized today per RA2302-5). This qualifies but does not overturn the handoff's "one key" recommendation: the handoff said rows 10 and 22 "differ only by a randomized Pre-Open second (:30 vs :38)"; in 2011-2012 CME published a difference of a full minute or two. One key is still right because no executable boundary ever diverged.

THE CHAIN AFTER 2011 IS EXHAUSTED. RA1106-4 (eff. 2011-07-11) is the first edition to drop the clock table, and RA1107-4/RA1108-4 (eff. 2011-11-07), RA1203-4R (eff. 2012-10-15), RA1303-4 (eff. 2013-03-18) and RA2302-5 (eff. 2023-07-31) state no per-product times at all.

U-0b IS CLOSED. CME's ContractSpecs for Henry Hub Look-Alike Last Day Financial (productId 2752) names ProductCode.TAS = "HHT" and states "TAS: Sunday - Friday 6:00 p.m. - 2:30 p.m. (5:00 p.m. - 1:30 p.m. CT)" - the CLT/NGT grid. HHT also appears as a Globex TAS contract in RA0907-4 (2009-08-31), which puts it in the family before the audit floor. Membership caveat worth a line beside the table: HHT is absent from every 2010-2011 MRAN per-root table (which list only CLT BZT BBT HOT NGT NNT RBT 7FT KTT CJT TTT YOT XKT XCT RET GCT SIT HGT), so its TAS eligibility lapses and returns - catalog data, not a family-schedule fact.

U-0a ONLY NARROWS. No CME document states MCT hours. MCL's ContractSpecs (productId 10037) names MCT as its TAS code but, uniquely among CL/HO/RB/BZ/NG/HH, its Globex Trading Hours row carries NO TAS line. What I did find is CME Globex Notice 2022-07-18, "Enable Trading At Settlement (TAS) Functionality for Micro Crude Oil Futures - August 6", whose table row is "Micro Crude Oil TAS | MCT | CT | 382" under the heading "iLink: tag 55-Symbol MDP 3.0 tag 1151 - Security Group". That places MCT in Globex security group CT - the crude-oil TAS group that carries CLT - which is the same kind of published-group-identity argument the handoff already uses for SYP/LBR ("one group cannot run two grids"). Its effective day is conditional ("pending completion of all regulatory review periods") so it dates nothing, and a member listing after the family clock began is caller-catalog data in any case. Parent's call: map MCT on group identity with the reasoning written down, or leave it UNMAPPED pending an hours statement.

GASOIL (7FT) IS FULLY DATED, AND THE HANDOFF'S "current close 10:30 CT is undated relative to those" IS WRONG - 11:30 a.m. ET IS 10:30 CT. The 2016-12-19 notice is the cutover, and I found a second CME source for it: the server-rendered 7F spec page reads "Trading in all TAS products will cease daily at 11:30 Standard Time (EST)" on the 2017-03-30 and 2017-11-29 captures, against "2:30 PM Eastern Time" on the 2016-09-25 capture. But note that 2016-09-25 value is itself generic boilerplate and wrong for 7F (RA1006-4 and the notice both say 12:00 p.m. ET at that date), which is exactly why the LIVE ContractSpecs TAS string for productId 2912 - "TAS: Sunday - Friday 5:00 p.m. - 1:30 p.m. CT", byte-identical to CL's - must not be read as a 7F statement. Record it as a source conflict and serve the sourced intersection 17:00 -> 10:30 CT.

ONE TRAP FOR U-4, FOUND HERE, WORTH CARRYING OVER: on the archived energy-hours page the TAS rows carry a "09:00-14:30 ET (08:00-13:30 CT)" column. That is the OPEN OUTCRY column - TAS was pit-eligible under Rule 524.A.1, and RA1006-4 separately says "Regular trading hours for open outcry trading in the Copper futures pit are from 8:10 a.m. until 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time". It is NOT a Globex RTH and must not be used to give globex_energy_tas a regular session.
